_schemaNote: Canonical misconception registry, derived from docs/foundation-release-1/MISCONCEPTION_MAP.md. Lessons reference these by id (array of strings) rather than copying the prose. Do not hand-edit id keys without updating every lesson that references them.

MC-COUNT-CORRESPONDENCE.label: Counting objects twice or skipping one
MC-COUNT-CORRESPONDENCE.likelyMentalModel: Treats counting as reciting a sequence of words alongside vague pointing, rather than a strict one-to-one match between each word and exactly one object.
MC-COUNT-CORRESPONDENCE.diagnosticQuestion: Can you touch each one as you say its number, just once?
MC-COUNT-CORRESPONDENCE.teacherResponse: Model moving each object to a "counted" pile while saying its number; have the learner repeat with the moving-aside physically enforced.

MC-CONSERVATION-REARRANGE.label: Thinking rearrangement changes quantity
MC-CONSERVATION-REARRANGE.likelyMentalModel: Judging quantity by the visual footprint (length, area, or spread) a group occupies, not by count — a normal developmental stage, not carelessness.
MC-CONSERVATION-REARRANGE.diagnosticQuestion: Did anyone add or take away any objects when I moved them?
MC-CONSERVATION-REARRANGE.teacherResponse: Have the learner do the rearranging themselves and predict the count before recounting, repeated across several rearrangements.

MC-DIGIT-VALUE-CONFUSION.label: Confusing the numeral with the quantity / place-value digit-value confusion
MC-DIGIT-VALUE-CONFUSION.likelyMentalModel: Numeral literacy (reading/writing the symbol) has outrun place-value understanding (what the symbol quantifies).
MC-DIGIT-VALUE-CONFUSION.diagnosticQuestion: Which part of '34' tells us the bundles? Which part tells us the loose ones?
MC-DIGIT-VALUE-CONFUSION.teacherResponse: Cover the numeral; ask the learner to state tens and ones from objects alone, then reveal the numeral and match each digit to what was just said.

MC-BOND-DIRECTION.label: Whole vs. part reversal (number-bond direction confusion)
MC-BOND-DIRECTION.likelyMentalModel: Relying on a bond diagram's spatial position (top/bottom, left/right) rather than the size relationship (the whole is always the sum of the parts).
MC-BOND-DIRECTION.diagnosticQuestion: Which number should be the biggest one here — the whole, or one of the parts?
MC-BOND-DIRECTION.teacherResponse: Ask the learner to add the two numbers they've called "parts" — does the sum match the number they've called "the whole"?

MC-MISSING-PART-ADD.label: Missing-part confusion (adding instead of finding the difference)
MC-MISSING-PART-ADD.likelyMentalModel: Over-applies "put together" (composing) reasoning to a "what's left" (decomposing) situation.
MC-MISSING-PART-ADD.diagnosticQuestion: If the whole is 8 and we already have 5, would the missing part be bigger or smaller than 8?
MC-MISSING-PART-ADD.teacherResponse: Before solving, ask the learner to predict whether the missing part will be larger or smaller than the given whole.

MC-MAKE10-SPLIT-ORDER.label: Make-10 decomposition errors (wrong split target or wrong add order)
MC-MAKE10-SPLIT-ORDER.likelyMentalModel: Has memorized "split one number into two pieces" as the action, without tracking which piece exists specifically to complete the benchmark.
MC-MAKE10-SPLIT-ORDER.diagnosticQuestion: Which piece did we split off to finish the ten? Let's add that piece first.
MC-MAKE10-SPLIT-ORDER.teacherResponse: Require the learner to say out loud, before adding anything, which piece will make a ten.

MC-COMPENSATE-UNBALANCED.label: Changing a number without compensating (compensation changing the answer)
MC-COMPENSATE-UNBALANCED.likelyMentalModel: Treats "make it friendlier" as the whole strategy, without tracking that a change made for ease must be paired with an equal-and-opposite change to preserve value.
MC-COMPENSATE-UNBALANCED.diagnosticQuestion: You changed one number — where did that same amount need to go to keep the total fair?
MC-COMPENSATE-UNBALANCED.teacherResponse: Have the learner compute the "friendlier" version and the original version by two independent methods and compare.

MC-ZERO-ONES-FAKE-ADDEND.label: Zero-ones confusion (fake + 0 addend in expanded form)
MC-ZERO-ONES-FAKE-ADDEND.likelyMentalModel: Pattern-matches the shape of expanded form (always two addends) rather than reasoning from each place's actual value.
MC-ZERO-ONES-FAKE-ADDEND.diagnosticQuestion: What is the value of the ones place here? If it's zero, do we need to write anything for it?
MC-ZERO-ONES-FAKE-ADDEND.teacherResponse: Ask the learner to physically point to the "zero ones" pile — when there's nothing there, ask whether writing "+ 0" adds anything real.

MC-NEARDOUBLE-DIRECTION.label: Near-double errors (wrong +1/-1 direction relative to a known double)
MC-NEARDOUBLE-DIRECTION.likelyMentalModel: Over-generalizes the first-learned adjustment direction as if it were universal, rather than re-checking each time.
MC-NEARDOUBLE-DIRECTION.diagnosticQuestion: Which double are we near, and is our number bigger or smaller than the double's matching part?
MC-NEARDOUBLE-DIRECTION.teacherResponse: Require the learner to state, before adjusting, whether the target number is one more or one less than the nearby double.
